newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS - Mexico's IMSA launches global IPO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mexico's IMSA launches global IPO.

text.p: Monterrey-based IMSA SA on Wednesday became the largest Mexican company to go public since the 1994 peso crisis, with the launch of a successful initial public offering in international and Mexican markets.

The family-owned industrial conglomerate placed 5.5 million American depository shares (ADS) in U.S., Canadian and European markets and an additional 18 million equity units, denominated as UBS shares, on the Mexican bourse. Nine local equity units equal one ADS, the company said.
IMSA's UBC shares finished the day on the Mexican bourse at 17 pesos per share, compared with an offer price of 16.63 pesos per share.
The company's ADR was the only Mexican issue that gained on Wall Street -- climbing from its offer price of $9 to $9-1/8.
"The market reacted well to the offer. We are very pleased," Eugenio Eloduy, IMSA's head of investor relations, told Reuters.

IMSA, which has interests in steel processing, automotive batteries and construction materials, raised about $142.5 million, $100 million of which will be used to redeem preferred stock and the remainder to pay off short-term debt.
The company's total debt after the move should stand at roughly $80 million, company officials said.
Dealers and analysts said the company, which also has battery operations in Argentina, Brazil, Venezuela and Puerto Rico, was priced at a premium but fairly.
"The stock is not coming cheap, but the shares are demanding the premium that they deserve," Alex Ryshawy, a steel analyst at DA Campbell in Los Angeles, told Reuters.
"It was priced pretty fairly," agreed Bond Snodgrass, an analyst at Abaco Brokerage in Mexico City. "Their steel processing business is a good business with high margins and a lot of growth."
Snodgrass estimated that the company's shares were trading at about 6.6 times 1996 earnings and about five times 1996 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.
